ELANCO RESTATEMENT — genuinely confirmed, with a real figure. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-17-analyzer-reset-master-plan.md (line 46) records: 'operating-income falls flagged LLY because of the Elanco divestiture' under an earlier, rejected purely-data-driven cyclicality test. This harness independently confirms the underlying distortion in LLY's own real NetIncomeLoss history: FY2018 net income 3232000000 (10-K accn 0000059478-19-000082) jumps to FY2019 8318400000 (10-K accn 0000059478-20-000057) then falls back to FY2020 6193700000 (10-K accn 0000059478-21-000083) — a jump-then-fall shape consistent with a one-time gain around Elanco Animal Health's September 2019 spin-off distorting the margin/income trend a naive year-over-year cyclicality or margin-decline check would read as a structural decline afterward. This is exactly why D1's chosen classifier is industry-code-based (SIC) rather than purely data-driven (revenue/margin trend) — confirmed by this harness's own cyclicalSic.ts design, not re-derived independently here. LLY has no us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss tag at all (see operatingIncomeNote above), so the 'operating-income falls' the master plan describes were read from a margin proxy this harness did not reconstruct; the net-income jump above is the closest real, independently-verified figure this harness could confirm from data.sec.gov.
